messages:
maria: Quick question — we should re-evaluate the prefill probing + KV-cache eviction interplay. Current autotuner does per-wave probes and sometimes evicts prefills mid-rollout which causes re-warmups and latency spikes. Any low-cost heuristics folks have used?

aj: We've seen regressions on long-tail seqs where the probe cost outweighs the kernel benefit. Short probes were triggering s128 kernels but the downstream batches ended up as s512, so wasted tokens + extra warmups.

kevin: Proposal: add a probe budget that's scoped by (model, route, deployment-tier) and tied to prefill TTL. If the prefill hit-rate > 80% for the route, skip probing. Hit-rate can be approximated from per-prefill metrics instead of exact counters.

sara: +1. Also consider probe modes: "probe-on-miss" vs "probe-ahead". For latency SLO paths, probe-ahead (in a low-sample fashion) can avoid first-request penalty, but it costs tokens. We need safe defaults per tier.

jun: How do we compute hit-rate cheaply? My take: derive from existing prometheus metrics like kv_prefill_hits_total / (kv_prefill_hits_total + kv_prefill_misses_total) with an EWMA to smooth spikes. Avoid storing per-request state.

aj: EWMA(60s) with alpha=0.2 worked for us in infra. Also add a tiny random probe sample (1%) to catch distribution shifts. If sample shows diff > 10% from EWMA, escalate full probe.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary started for autotune/probe-better-ttl (canary id: can-821). 3 nodes in cluster alpha.

kevin: Important edge: kernel selection must consider candidate batchshapes. If probe only evaluates a single common batchshape, it may pick a kernel that underperforms when actual batchshape distribution changes. Suggest multi-shape probing: probe for {s128,s256,s512} with capped budget.

maria: Sketch of a tiny probe API we could add to the runtime (idea):
```
POST /internal/autotune/probe 
body: {"model":"redwood-13b","route":"chat.default","candidates":[128,256,512],"budget_tokens":20000} 
returns: {"best_shape":256,"metrics":{"lat_95_ms":42,"tokens_used":1834}}
```
We'd run this only when route-level heuristics say it's allowed.

sara: Agree on budget controls. Suggest default params: probe_budget_tokens=50k per GPU per minute, probe_sample_rate=0.01, prefill_ttl=300s. Also clamp per-model because small models should have much smaller budgets.

jun: Experiment plan: A/B canary 5% traffic with logs that include tag `probe_decision` and `prefill_evicted` to verify we don't thrash. Track 95/99 lat, token cost, and prefilling hit-rate delta.

aj: Sounds good. I'll draft a short RFC with metrics we should collect and the canary rollout plan. @maria do you want kernel autotuner metrics schema (which fields we log) in the RFC?

maria: Yes please include the schema. Also add a section on graceful fallback: if probe fails or budget exhausted, prefer a safer, broader kernel (e.g., favor s256 over s128 for mixed traffic).

kevin: One more: eviction policy tweak — prefer LRU that is aware of probe-created prefills (mark them as immutable for TTL so we don't evict them for a short window) to avoid immediate re-probing. We'll prototype in the canary.

maria: Thanks everyone — looks like action items: aj RFC + metrics schema, kevin prototype for multi-shape probing + soft-immute prefills, jun experiment dashboard, sara will vet budget defaults. I'll sync w/ product on SLO tradeoffs and log results next sync.
